picks.why: A concrete CPU co-design account separates held-out workloads and pre-silicon power from the limits of its undisclosed comparison core.
The gap between average criteria and strict success exposes nearly correct integrations, with judging and timeout limits stated.
A synthetic web supports repeatable adversarial tests without confusing test volume with proof that real browsing is safe.
Typed extraction models come with internal-evaluation caveats and a preview-endpoint change that matters to existing users.
An institutional review announcement keeps a high-profile complexity claim conditional rather than treating announced results as accepted proofs.
